title: How do you compute the frequency (count) of each string in a list using streams?
shortTitle: Frequency count of each string in a list using streams
keyPoints: groupingBy(identity(), counting()) produces Map<String, Long> with frequency of each string
TreeMap::new as the map factory produces sorted keys automatically
sorted(comparingByValue().reversed()) on the entrySet ranks strings by frequency descending
For case-insensitive counting, add map(String::toLowerCase) before groupingBy
This replaces the manual pattern of map.merge(key, 1L, Long::sum) in a for-loop
The counting() collector is more efficient than toList() followed by size() because it only tracks a counter

s1_definition.oneliner: Use groupingBy(Function.identity(), Collectors.counting()) to produce a Map<String, Long> with the frequency of each string in the list.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **groupingBy(identity(), counting())** groups strings by their value and counts occurrences, producing `Map<String, Long>`.
- **TreeMap::new** as the map factory produces alphabetically sorted keys without a separate sort step.
- **sorted(comparingByValue().reversed())** on the entry set produces a frequency-ranked list from most common to least.
- **map(String::toLowerCase)** before groupingBy enables case-insensitive counting.
- This single collector call replaces the verbose manual pattern of iterating with `map.merge(key, 1L, Long::sum)`.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, the operations team logs every transaction type in a day: ["NEFT", "UPI", "NEFT", "RTGS", "UPI", "NEFT"]. At end of day, they need a summary: NEFT appeared 3 times, UPI appeared 2 times, RTGS appeared 1 time. The groupingBy plus counting collector produces this summary in one pass.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  ["NEFT", "UPI", "NEFT", "RTGS", "UPI", "NEFT"]
       │
       ▼
  groupingBy(identity(), counting())
       │
       ▼
  Map<String, Long>
  ┌───────────────┐
  │ NEFT  → 3     │
  │ UPI   → 2     │
  │ RTGS  → 1     │
  └───────┬───────┘
          │
          ▼
  sorted(comparingByValue().reversed())
          │
          ▼
  [NEFT:3, UPI:2, RTGS:1]  (frequency ranked)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
String frequency counting is one of the most common stream interview questions. The answer is always `groupingBy(Function.identity(), Collectors.counting())` which produces `Map<String, Long>`. For sorted keys, pass `TreeMap::new` as the map factory. For frequency-ranked output, stream the entrySet and sort by value descending.

This single-line collector replaces the manual pattern of iterating with `map.merge(key, 1L, Long::sum)`. For case-insensitive counting, add `map(String::toLowerCase)` before groupingBy.

At National Bank of India, the operations dashboard shows transaction type volumes: NEFT (3 times), UPI (2 times), RTGS (1 time). The groupingBy collector produces this summary in one pass through the data.

Remember one sentence: groupingBy with identity and counting is the one-liner for frequency maps, and TreeMap gives sorted keys.
